te: Meeting summary video · Hospital finances (continued): hearing the association of regional and general hospitals and hospitals in the field
Finances of Ministry of Public Health hospitals, 2023–2025
se: The committee considered the finances of hospitals under the Ministry of Public Health over the past 3 years, inviting representatives of the Permanent Secretary of Public Health and the Health Economics and Health Security Division. The main problem is that income does not match costs, while older persons and patients with chronic diseases are increasing and some reimbursement rates still do not reflect real costs, so many hospitals have negative maintenance funds, affecting cash flow and the continuity of services. The ministry has made financial management more integrated, such as taking part in allocating the National Health Security Fund in 2026 and using a financial crisis scale of 0–7 with an early warning system.
it: Finances of hospitals under the Ministry of Public Health (fiscal years 2023–2025) and solutions

te: Meeting summary video · Finances of Ministry of Public Health hospitals, 2023–2025
Preparing the forum “The Facts on the Gold Card Bill | What Does the Committee Say?” part 2
se: This meeting was moved from 28 to 29 September 2026. The committee reviewed part 1 of the forum, “Improving the Gold Card Law: Intent, Facts and What People Should Know” (23 Sep 2026), and agreed to hold part 2 on restructuring the board and participation before benefits are set, using the PCV vaccine and gender-affirming hormones as case studies. Suggestions included dividing the forum into 2 sessions and moving the board structure topic to the next event, improving the picture and sound of the live broadcast, and making invitation materials easier to understand.
it: Holding the forum “The Facts on the Gold Card Bill | What Does the Committee Say?” part 2

te: Reforming the state workforce under the OCSC letter: concerns of public health staff
se: The committee considered the approach to reforming the management of the state workforce under the letter of the Office of the Civil Service Commission (4 Sep 2026) and its effects on the positions, careers and staffing of public health personnel. Representatives of 15 staff associations said the announcement made staff worried and lowered morale. Promotion submissions made since 2024 are still delayed, while several professions face serious shortages, such as radiologic technologists, medical technologists, Thai traditional medicine practitioners and registered nurses. They proposed finishing the promotion assessments pending from 2024 within fiscal year 2026, reviewing the circular letter, and developing career paths that match the real workload. A representative of the OCSC explained the reasons for and approach of the measures.
it: Approach to reforming state workforce management (OCSC letter of 4 Sep 2026) and its effects on public health personnel

te: Protecting policy from tobacco industry interference: hearing the Department of Disease Control
se: The committee considered Thailand's situation and approach in following Article 5.3 of the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control. The Department of Disease Control explained that it has a 2012 department regulation on contact with tobacco operators, requiring contact only as necessary, transparent and open to checking, preventing conflicts of interest, and refusing sponsorship from the tobacco industry. Its limits are that the regulation applies only to the Department of Disease Control, not yet to other agencies such as the Excise Department, and has no penalties. The department will therefore prepare guidelines against interference for state agencies, and push through the National Tobacco Products Control Committee for a regulation of the Office of the Prime Minister on this matter.
it: Situation and approach in following Article 5.3 of the tobacco control convention (Department of Disease Control)

te: Making Parliament's rules consistent with the tobacco control convention
se: Meeting on Tuesday 8 September 2026, according to the meeting notice. The agenda was a study of ways to bring Parliament's regulations in line with obligations under the tobacco control convention (Article 5.3 of the WHO Framework Convention on Tobacco Control, on protecting policy from interference by the tobacco industry), including problems and obstacles, with academic experts invited to give information. (The Senate published the meeting summary as an image file. Please read the details in the original documents below.)
it: Bringing Parliament's regulations in line with the tobacco control convention (WHO FCTC Article 5.3)

te: Report on reforming health insurance: prices at real cost, separate staff budget and a national basic benefit package
se: The committee considered the draft report of the Subcommittee to Study the Budget System, Management and Good Governance under the National Health Security System. Key proposals are: adjust inpatient reference prices to reflect real costs and review them every 2 years; separate the staff budget from the capitation budget and allocate service budgets by actual tasks and workload; set a national basic service package that everyone receives equally, with possible voluntary co-payment for services beyond it without affecting people on low incomes and vulnerable groups; and improve governance, such as the make-up of the board, terms of no more than 2, and protection for staff. The work is planned in 3 phases, from gathering information and public hearings to enforcing the law.
it: Draft study report of the Subcommittee to Study the Budget System, Management and Good Governance

te: Report on the Thai traditional medicine bill with 6 proposals, and a report on primary health care work
se: The committee considered the draft study report on the Protection and Promotion of Thai Traditional Medicinal Intelligence Bill, with 6 proposals, such as: common herbal formulas used in many areas should not be monopolised by any one community but should be national formulas; speeding up the survey and registration of herb-growing areas as protected areas; building a digital database of traditional knowledge for patent offices around the world to check (as in India); using the fund to support research and to bring herbal medicines into the National List of Essential Medicines; defining “community” clearly and giving it legal status; and coordinating policy between ministries. It also considered the draft report on primary health care work of the subcommittee concerned.
it: Draft study report on the Protection and Promotion of Thai Traditional Medicinal Intelligence Bill (rule 119)
Draft report on primary health care work (primary health care subcommittee)

te: Study of the amended bill to protect and promote Thai traditional medicine wisdom
se: The committee studied the Protection and Promotion of Thai Traditional Medicinal Intelligence Bill (No. ..) under rule 119 of the Rules of Procedure of the Senate, inviting the Department of Thai Traditional and Alternative Medicine and the Office of the Council of State. It has 3 main points: communities may register together as owners of traditional knowledge, and if a community ceases to exist the knowledge is protected as national knowledge; commercial use of the knowledge is adjusted and sources of income for the Thai traditional medicine wisdom fund are added; and the Director-General may grant permission and settle fines, with heavier penalties for commercial use without permission. A representative of the Council of State observed that recognising community rights may add paperwork, and suggested community representatives and benefit sharing.
it: Protection and Promotion of Thai Traditional Medicinal Intelligence Bill (No. ..) B.E. .... (rule 119)

te: Gender-affirming hormones (continued): the NHSO explains how benefits are set
se: The committee heard the Secretary-General of the National Health Security Office, who explained that section 5 of the National Health Security Act B.E. 2002 covers treatment, health promotion and disease prevention, and that the 2022 announcement on the scope of services uses an exclusion principle: services not excluded are benefits, except procedures for appearance without a medical indication or treatments still being tested. The NHSO reviews benefits every year by assessing safety and value for money (HTA), and the National Health Security Board also considers ethics, the readiness of services and quality of life when deciding.
it: Setting the gender-affirming hormone benefit in the National Health Security system (NHSO Secretary-General)

te: Gender-affirming hormones (continued): views of the royal colleges of physicians
se: The committee continued to consider providing gender-affirming hormones as a benefit, covering criteria, clinical practice guidelines, safety and budget. The Royal College of Physicians of Thailand confirmed that it is a necessary medical service that must follow professional standards with continuous assessment and follow-up, and proposed national clinical practice guidelines made with multiple professions and a registry for long-term follow-up. The Royal College of Pediatricians of Thailand made observations on services for children and adolescents, long-term health effects, and mental and psychosocial care. The Royal College of Psychiatrists of Thailand said that gender identity is not an illness, but some people with gender incongruence need hormones, and adolescents must be assessed in all respects.
it: Providing gender-affirming hormones as a benefit: criteria, clinical practice guidelines, safety and budget

te: New National Health Security Bill drafted by the subcommittee
se: The committee considered the National Health Security Bill B.E. ...., drafted by the working group of the subcommittee on budget and good governance together with representatives of the Office of the Council of State, based on agencies' comments and public hearings in all 4 regions. The main change is to move from a clear split between purchasers and providers of services to joint management that defines the roles of purchasers, providers and regulators clearly and has them work together from the start. Benefits are divided into 3 levels: essential basic services, extra services specific to each fund, and other services for which users may co-pay voluntarily. The announcement on the scope of basic services is to be reviewed every 3 years, and the membership of the National Health Security Board balanced between fund administrators and experts, service users, and service providers. The committee also set the issues for hearing the views of the public and agencies.
it: National Health Security Bill B.E. .... and issues for the public hearing

te: Gender-affirming hormones in the gold card scheme
se: The committee studied adding gender-affirming hormones as a benefit in the National Health Security system, covering criteria, the readiness of services, safety and budget impact. The NHSO explained that the work has developed since 2020. These hormone medicines are already in the National List of Essential Medicines, so they can be a basic service, covering people aged 18 and over who need them, so that they receive the medicines correctly. The National Health Security Board approved them as a health promotion and disease prevention benefit.
it: Adding gender-affirming hormones as a National Health Security benefit (NHSO)

te: Following emerging diseases: hantavirus, Ebola and COVID-19
se: The committee followed the situation of emerging infectious diseases. The Department of Disease Control reported that the Andes strain of hantavirus that spread on a cruise ship can pass from person to person, with an incubation period of 1–8 weeks and early symptoms like influenza. Thailand has found no patients yet, but has raised it to the 14th dangerous communicable disease under the Communicable Diseases Act B.E. 2015, with measures in 4 areas: screening travellers from risk countries, preparing laboratories for confirmation tests, rehearsing plans to receive suspected patients, and communicating to prevent false news. Ebola has been found in Africa, and Thailand has found no infected persons.
it: Situation of Ebola, hantavirus and COVID-19 and the effects on Thailand
